fields.reasoning: Intent: the sibling change sets carved out of accepted umbrellas this session (code anchors 01M6HJX, unclaimed changes 01M6HKR) both serve model-tells-truth, and text-references' own statement (a rename never breaks a sentence) is about the model staying true; anyone-builds is the umbrella's broader root and adds nothing here. The carving guide says carve keeps IDs and links and that an emptied source is withdrawn by hand, and references-by-id is landed so the decided-by link applies in the target. Stored form: references-by-id says stored by ID, shown by handle; a bracketed @{ID} cannot collide with the '@' already in the log (emails, checkout@v7, '@key'), and requiring whitespace or ( [ before @ keeps those three from being read as references even on new writes. Verbatim fields are skipped because the hard rule is never to alter an owner's exact words, and sources are scrubbed transcripts. Refusing an unresolvable reference mirrors how a link to a node the write may not see is refused, and keeps a dangling reference from ever being written; @@ gives an escape so a literal @word can still be written. Showing by current handle in both text and JSON makes output round-trip through a later write. A missing node in check is a fail because the capability exists so sentences never break, while a retired target is still a real node, so only a warn.
fields.statement: (1) Intent and leaf: the change set serves the landed root intent model-tells-truth, and the leaf comes over with rhiza carve text-references --from 01M5SWSWDVB237 --to 01M6HNNWFR1J2AHQRNKFTPME46, which keeps its ID and moves its decided-by link to references-by-id; the umbrella, left with no ops, is withdrawn. (2) Stored form and scanned fields: a write (node add or set) scans every string-valued field of a node, except the verbatim fields quote, quote_where and wording and every field of a source node, which are stored exactly as given. A reference starts with @ at the start of the text or after whitespace or an opening ( or [, followed by a handle (lower-case words joined by dashes) or a node ID or unique ID prefix of 4+ characters; so emails, checkout@v7 and a quoted '@key' are not references. @@ writes a literal @ and is never resolved. Each reference is stored as @{<full node ID>}; json_fields and links are not scanned. Already-landed entries are never rewritten. (3) Unresolvable reference: the write is refused whole (not found, exit 4), naming each reference that names no node the write may refer to; the rule is the same as for a link's ends: landed nodes and nodes of the write's own change set, live and not retired. The error's next says to fix the handle or write @@ for a literal @. (4) Display and check: render, show, why, slice and the read apps (text and --json alike) show each @{ID} as @<the node's current handle> in that view, so the shown text written back resolves to the same IDs; a reference that does not resolve in the view is shown as @{<full ID>}. rhiza check scans the folded model's stored references, each in the view of the change set that wrote it: an ID that names no node is a fail finding (a dangling reference), naming the node, field and ID; an ID that names a retired node is a warn.
